purpose: Standard mid-size laptop-grade model coverage for proving zgml against PyTorch beyond tiny synthetic and SmolLM-only benchmarks.

pr.description: Cheap enough for routine PR evidence; must stay green before claiming the suite is healthy.

laptop_core.description: The main local-workstation proof: real models that should fit and run on a modern laptop without cloud hardware.

frontier.description: Strategic model families that define missing compiler/runtime work before they become required gates.

benchmark.metric: prompt/decode tok/s vs PyTorch Transformers, plus secondary llama.cpp percentage
benchmark.gate: executable today against llama.cpp; PyTorch reference harness required before suite-ready

models.why: Keeps the current executable-stencil LLM path cheap while making PyTorch the promotion target.

benchmark.metric: probe coverage now; prompt/decode tok/s, memory peak, logits/prediction agreement vs PyTorch once executable
benchmark.gate: must move from LLaMA-family probe-only to load/compile from PyTorch-compatible weights; performance target starts at PyTorch parity

models.why: First step above toy scale while still fast enough for frequent laptop runs.

benchmark.metric: prompt/decode tok/s, KV-cache bytes, cold-load ms, hot session step ms, agreement vs PyTorch
benchmark.gate: must compile/load from PyTorch-compatible weights; performance target starts at PyTorch parity

models.why: A real laptop-sized assistant model that should expose cache, allocator, and command-scheduling costs.

models.architecture: Qwen3 decoder-only transformer with Q/K norm coverage

benchmark.metric: prompt/decode tok/s, architecture feature coverage, agreement vs PyTorch
benchmark.gate: must probe architecture metadata and match PyTorch logits before execution becomes required

models.why: Prevents overfitting the runtime to one LLaMA-family checkpoint shape.

models.architecture: Qwen3 decoder-only transformer with Q/K norm coverage

benchmark.metric: prompt/decode tok/s, memory peak, shape-specialization cache reuse, agreement vs PyTorch

models.why: Mid-size architecture diversity at a scale where laptop memory pressure starts to matter.

benchmark.metric: loader/probe support first, then prompt/decode tok/s and agreement vs PyTorch
benchmark.gate: not required until Phi architecture metadata and op coverage exist

models.why: Useful negative/control target for proving the model loader generalizes beyond LLaMA/Qwen/SmolLM.

models.model: DistilBERT SST-2 or equivalent ONNX/safetensors export

benchmark.metric: sentences/s, p50/p95 ms, max_abs_diff vs reference logits
benchmark.gate: front-end graph import and encoder attention support required

models.why: Covers bidirectional attention, classifier heads, and the non-generative ML use case.

benchmark.metric: images/s, p50/p95 ms, top-1 agreement, max_abs_diff
benchmark.gate: depthwise/grouped conv, batchnorm folding, and resize/preprocess story required

models.why: Laptop AI is not only token generation; this catches CNN and image-preprocess gaps.

benchmark.metric: image embeddings/s, text embeddings/s, cosine agreement
benchmark.gate: ViT patch embed, encoder stack, normalization, and tokenizer story required

models.why: Forces the library to handle real embedding workflows and multimodal tensor shapes.

benchmark.metric: latent-to-image ms, max_abs_diff or image metric vs reference

models.why: Smallest useful diffusion-adjacent target; catches image decoder kernels before full UNet.

models.model: Stable Diffusion 1.5 UNet single denoise step

benchmark.metric: one denoise step ms at 512x512 latent size, memory peak, numeric/image agreement
benchmark.gate: frontier until attention, conv, norm, and scheduler inputs are modeled

models.why: The canonical laptop diffusion workload, but too broad to make a first required gate.

benchmark.metric: audio seconds/s, encoder ms, decoder token/s, transcript agreement
benchmark.gate: mel feature pipeline, encoder-decoder attention, and tokenizer/decoder loop required

models.why: Voice is a different host/runtime shape: streaming-ish input, encoder cache, decoder loop.

benchmark.metric: audio seconds/s, memory peak, transcript agreement

models.why: A mid-size voice model after the tiny path is technically proven.

promotionPolicy: A model starts as unsupported-target until loader/probe evidence exists.
A target moves to next when it can load, compile/probe, and produce a reference-comparable output shape.
A target moves to ready only after a checked PyTorch benchmark artifact captures speed, memory, and numeric or task-level correctness.
Only ready models can become required PR gates; laptop_core models should become nightly or manual release gates first.
